about: Player-facing presentation of extracted fields (ADR-0002 §2-§3). Reviewed data, not a run-time gate. Fields not listed are technical. Each decision cites the code that reads the field; see docs/adr/0002-player-template-and-guides.md.

game_text.about: Labels named {"game": KEY} are read per snapshot from the capture's item-tooltip text object (dynamicTooltip in UI.decompiled.cs) and localized Language_Mgr keys. English only; a trailing ': ' is removed. If the key is missing in a capture, the fallback label is used and the audit reports it.

formats.integer: Round half away from zero to a whole number; thousands separator.
formats.round2: Round to 2 decimal places like the game's Math.Round(x, 2); drop trailing zeros.
formats.percent: x * 100, rounded to 2 places, then '%'. Used where the game's tooltip shows a percentage.
formats.range: Object {x, y}: 'x–y', or just 'x' when equal.
formats.signed_text: String as stored; the game shows these with their sign, e.g. '+10'.
formats.per_minute_from_seconds: 60 / x shots per minute, rounded to a whole number, then ' / min'.
formats.positive_integer: abs(x) rounded to a whole number.
formats.coded: The coded value's readable label from fact_labels, else the raw value.
formats.flag: The label alone, with no value; used for yes-only traits such as Harvest.
formats.repair_link: Name of the repair-item relationship target; omitted when there is none.
formats.handmade_ammo: Handmade ammo modifiers: damage −%, range −%, recoil +%, dud %, jam %, neutral values hidden (phase 3).

names.about: Distinct player names for records that share a display name (ADR-0002 §3). Rules apply in order; the first that makes names unique within the topic and kind wins. Implemented in phase 2, extended by phase 3 joins.

rules.description: Suffix by how the record is obtained when that differs: '(crafted)' when a recipe produces it, '(loot)' when only loot or merchants provide it.
Building materials: suffix the block shape from the record's tooltip text object name, e.g. 7_5_Block_1.4_Obsidian_Tooltip → 'Block 1/4'.
Otherwise suffix the first player-tier stat that differs, e.g. 'Military Helmet (Durability 600)'.
Last resort: '(variant N)' in stable key order, reported by the audit.

sources.about: Where a readable name comes from when the record name is internal. Game text wins; wiki names are used only where the game shows none, and pages say so.

workbench.how: The bench prefab's Language_Text title object (e.g. 'Cutting Workbench', 'Gunsmith Workbench', 'Anvil', 'Furnace'). The craft window title is baked in each bench prefab (UI.decompiled.cs declares _CraftWindow_Title but never assigns it).

skill.how: Skill_Mgr.AllSkill _name / _instruct Language_Text; the description's {0}-style placeholders are filled per level from _values[level-1]._replaceStrs (Creature.decompiled.cs ~12381, Replace_One_By_One).

creature.how: The game shows no creature names (no nameplate, no kill log). Pattern Z_Man_N → 'Male zombie (type N)', Z_Woman_N → 'Female zombie (type N)', names containing ZBoss → 'Boss zombie (type N)'. Pages mark these as wiki names.

biome.how: The game shows no biome names (Merchant_Mgr.GetBiomeNameFromHit is internal only). Wiki names keyed by the biome record name, worded after the terrain bundle (terrain_mossy_forest, terrain_tropical_swamp); pages mark them as such. The near-spawn Base ground is "Spawn area", because players read "Base" as their own base.
